title: corpus.json — benchmark corpus case manifest
description: One benchmark corpus manifest, checked in as bench/corpus/<id>/case.json and copied into a run bundle as .review/corpus-*/corpus.json. The case records the ground truth a review output is graded against: a real PR that later needed a bug-fix commit, or a seeded defect with what was injected. calibrate and trend join findings.json against these bugs offline; matching is path plus a +/- line_tolerance window, one finding per bug. additionalProperties stays closed so a typo fails validation instead of silently grading a different field.

id.description: Stable case id, matching the bench/corpus/<id> directory name.

kind.description: seeded for deterministic injected fixtures, real for a published PR with a later fix.

line_tolerance.description: How many lines from a bug still count as the same defect (default 3). A hit is one-to-one: a second finding on the same bug is a false positive.

provenance.description: Where the case came from: injected text for seeded cases, or repo/PR/fix_commit for real ones. The validation test enforces the per-kind requirements the schema cannot express.

bugs.description: At least one known defect. path, line, kind, and severity are the published ground truth; matching uses path plus the line window, not kind or severity.

provenance.description: Case origin. Seeded cases name what was injected; real cases name the repository, PR number, and the later commit that fixed the bug.

bug.description: One known defect: the reviewed path, the line in the reviewed head, the defect kind (off-by-one, nil-deref, injection, missing-error-check, ...), and the severity a good review should assign.
